yudhishthira.q: Day after day countless creatures are going to the abode of Yama, yet those that remain behind believe themselves to be immortal. What can be more wonderful than this?
yudhishthira.w: Answering the Yaksha at the lake

yudhishthira.q: O great Indra, I shall not abandon this dog today from desire of my happiness.
yudhishthira.w: At the gate of heaven, refusing to leave the dog that followed him

draupadi.q: Go, and ask that gambler present in the assembly, whom he hath lost first, himself, or me.
draupadi.w: To the messenger sent to fetch her to the dice hall

bhima.q: The earth shall drink the blood of Duryodhana, and Karna, and the wicked Sakuni, and Dussasana that maketh the fourth.
bhima.w: Leaving for exile after the dice game

arjuna.q: I wish not to slay these though they slay me, O slayer of Madhu, even for the sake of the sovereignty of the three worlds, what then for the sake of (this) earth?
arjuna.w: To Krishna, as the armies stood ready at Kurukshetra

krishna.q: Whenever, O Bharata, loss of piety and the rise of impiety occurreth, on those occasions do I create myself. For the protection of the righteous and for the destruction of the evil doers, for the sake of establishing Piety, I am born age after age.

duryodhana.q: As long as I live, even that much of our land which may be covered by the point of a sharp needle shall not, O Madhava, be given by us unto the Pandavas.

bhishma.q: O fisherman, from this day I adopt the vow of Brahmacharya (study and meditation in celibacy).
bhishma.w: To Satyavati’s father, so that Shantanu might marry her

karna.q: O famous lady, the number of thy sons will never be less than five. Five it will always be,—either with me, or with Arjuna, and myself slain.
karna.w: To Kunti, when she revealed that she was his mother

drona.q: I should like then to have the thumb of thy right hand.
drona.w: To Ekalavya, asking his teacher’s fee

gandhari.q: Since thou wert indifferent to the Kurus and the Pandavas whilst they slew each other, therefore, O Govinda, thou shalt be the slayer of thy own kinsmen!
gandhari.w: Cursing Krishna on the battlefield after the war
